Weeklies is for planning meals once, then not asking yourself what to eat every day. Your week runs Monday through Sunday and repeats every week. Today\'s recipe sits in the green card at the top of the Week tab, with a button to add it to the shopping list; tap any other day to choose a recipe or change it whenever your plans change.

Recipes are for meals you already know how to cook. Store the ingredients for one portion, one line at a time, and optionally the instructions. Open the Recipes tab to add, search, review, or remove saved meals.

To edit a recipe, open it from the list and tap the pencil. The form is the same as for a new recipe, with your current name and ingredients filled in; saving replaces that recipe and keeps the same entry everywhere it is used in your plan. Tap Scale on a recipe to view its amounts multiplied or divided, or to save the scaled amounts to the recipe. The bin icon deletes a recipe.
Import (Recipes tab) reads recipe data from JSON-LD on the page — no API key needed. Enter a recipe URL; ingredient amounts are scaled to one portion before saving. You review and edit before saving.

Import with AI uses your Mistral API key (Settings → Recipe import) to extract the recipe when schema data is missing or incomplete. The key stays on this device and is not included in backup files. Same URL input as Import; requires an internet connection.

Type in the Add an item row and press Done to add a line. Tap an item to put it in the basket; tap it again to bring it back. Clear empties the basket. Add today\'s recipe adds the ingredients of whatever recipe is planned for today on the Week tab, and Add recipe adds any recipe; you choose the number of portions each time, starting from Portions per day in Settings (each number in an ingredient line is multiplied by that value).
Turn dark mode on or off; the choice is remembered after you close the app.
Portions per day is the multiplier used when you use Add today\'s recipe on the shopping list: every numeric quantity in each ingredient line is multiplied by this value.
Recipe import: add your Mistral API key under Recipe import. It is stored locally and excluded from backup export and import.
This Help screen is linked from Settings.

Weeklies is fully local and completely offline. Recipes, your weekly plan, and the shopping list are stored on this device, where they stay until you remove them in the app or replace them by importing a backup.

In Settings, open the Backups section. Export file writes one JSON file (default name like weeklies-backup-2026-05-09.json) containing recipes, your weekly plan, the shopping list, and settings — including dark mode and portions per day.
Import replaces all stored data with the contents of that file. Nothing is merged with what you already had — confirm only when you intend to overwrite the app completely.

Weeklies stores your data on your device. The app has no accounts, no analytics, no advertising, and no tracking. It does not send your data anywhere unless you use the optional AI recipe import described below.

Your recipes, weekly plan, shopping list, and settings (dark mode, portions per day) are saved in local storage on this device only. They stay there until you delete them in the app or replace them by importing a backup file. This data is never transmitted to us or to any server.

Export (Settings → Data) writes a JSON file to a location you choose. The file is yours: the app never uploads it, and the app has no access to any other files on your device. Import reads only the backup file you pick, and replaces your stored data with its contents.

Import fetches the recipe page from the web address you enter, on your device, and reads the recipe data from the page itself. The request goes directly to that website, the same as opening it in a browser.

Import with AI is optional and only runs when you ask for it. It sends the recipe web address or page text you provide to the Mistral AI API (api.mistral.ai) using your own API key, so the recipe can be extracted when the page does not contain structured recipe data. Your API key is stored on this device only and is never included in backup exports. These requests are processed by Mistral according to Mistral\'s privacy policy; we do not see them and cannot access your key. Without this feature, the app makes no network requests at all.
The app can open the system file picker when you export or import a backup, and only for the file or folder you select. It requests no other permissions.
Weeklies is a general-purpose meal planner and is not directed at children. Because the app collects no personal data, no age verification is used.
If the app changes in a way that affects your privacy, this policy will be updated and published with the matching app update. The current version is always available on GitHub and inside the app.
Questions about this policy can be raised on GitHub: github.com/ConorRyan/weeklies.
